title: Restore one dirty 679-owner scalar in both orientations and price its receipt
body:
One named dirty retirement is clean in each direction with restored independent escrow and the two exact 679-owner operators. The repair pays three grade-seven contacts per call.

## Scope and source

Uses the two-hole #7950 word and fixes all other operations. Scalar MOVE updates chart tags; the physical chart operation and 3,550 other dirty retirements remain open. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit679-one-owned-retirement/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. `python3 -I -B verify.py` passed from a clean copy, including 86 adjoint donor identities, affected readers, escrows and corruption. The first-trial signed change is about −785.589754. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Bind the physical transport or find a cheaper local reader and price the full cleanup schedule.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
